verses.1: And you also, O kings and princes, do not walk in his ways, but fear God, who created you and has kept you until now.
verses.3: For Balak the son of Zippor, when the children of Israel came from the land of Amalek, that they might inherit the land of the Canaanites, the Hittites, and the Perizzites.
verses.4: And he said to Balaam, 'I beg you, interpret for me; for whomever you curse is cursed, and whomever you bless is blessed, and I will give you much gold and silver that will honor you; interpret for me, I pray.'
verses.5: And Balaam came, walking and pondering his divination, and Balak the son of Zippor showed him where the children of Israel were encamped.
verses.6: And he made divinations and offered sacrifices, and slaughtered sheep and cattle from among their flocks, and he wished to curse the children of Israel.
verses.7: But God was not willing that he should curse them; rather, He turned the curse into a blessing by his word.
verses.8: And He said, 'Those who bless you shall be blessed, and those who curse you shall be cursed, for you are the people whom God has chosen, and you are the dwelling place of the Beloved who shall come from heaven.'
verses.9: And because of this Balak the son of Zippor was grieved, and was troubled and angry, because he had blessed them before him when he had commanded him to curse them.
verses.10: And Balaam said to him, 'I cannot curse those whom God has blessed, for they are a people whom God has chosen, who have come into this land.'
verses.11: And Balak the son of Zippor said to Balaam, 'I wanted you to curse them for me, but you did not curse them; instead you blessed them before me. And I would have filled your house with gold and silver, which I would have given you if you had said, "Give me," and had cursed them for me. But you blessed them and did me no good, and neither will I do good to you.'
verses.12: And Balaam said, 'I cannot transgress or go beyond the word of God; but whatever word God puts in my mouth, that I will speak.'
verses.13: And I will not defraud my soul of my wealth; for if I loved wealth, God would rebuke me, so that I would not curse a blessed people.
verses.14: For God said to Jacob their father, "Those who bless you shall be blessed, and those who curse you shall be cursed, for everyone who blesses you is blessed."
verses.15: And whoever curses you without cause is cursed. Make your deeds and your ways good, so that God may prosper you.
verses.16: And do not be like the former people who provoked God with their evil deeds, and He was angry with them; and there were those whom He destroyed by the water of the flood.
verses.17: And there were those whom He destroyed by the hand of their enemies, and He brought an evil people against them, who put them to death and made war upon their kings, together with their prophets and their Levites.
verses.18: And they carried them away to a foreign land which they did not know, and they made war upon them, and afflicted them, and oppressed them, and laid waste their land.
verses.19: And they left Jerusalem desolate, like a plowed field, for they set up a garrison and a fortress against the holy city.
verses.20: And the priests were made war upon, and the law was abolished, and their hands fell slack.
verses.21: And the Hebrew women were made war upon, and they did not weep for their dead who had died, for they were made war upon and were in distress.
verses.22: And the children wept, and the old men were put to shame, and they had no mercy on the face of the aged and the gray-haired.
verses.23: And there was no one in the assembly, and they spared no one, and they laid waste all whom they found in their cities, and they carried them away captive to a foreign land which they did not know. For when God willed to be angry with His people, He first removed His sanctuary.
verses.24: And because of this, when God was angry with the children of Israel, God forsook Jerusalem, and it was plowed like a field, because at all times they provoked their Creator.
verses.25: Yet He did not destroy them utterly, for He had mercy on them for the sake of their fathers, and not because of their own righteousness did He have mercy on them, but because He loved their fathers—Abraham, Isaac, and Jacob—who reigned in righteousness and walked uprightly before their Creator.
verses.26: And He also established their name as a memorial of honor, both in heaven and on earth.
verses.27: And likewise you also, O kings and princes who are in this passing world, remember those who were before you, who walked in purity, so that they inherited the kingdom of heaven and their name was made good for generation after generation.
verses.28: And you also, so that your kingdom may be upright and your name made good, like the good kings who were before you, who pleased God in the goodness of their lives.
